title: The option-key guard misses some waiting-page writes, and the page's none-key block does not name the option
why: Named incident, Nov 2 12:15 and 12:25 CST, Home waiting page: decisions duo-search-top and climate-purifier-preset were written with an option keyed none. The write went through. The page then blocked each item with 'An option of this decision uses the key none', and the owner had to ask what was wrong. Fixed by renaming the keys. Reported by the Home session; owner brought it to triage Nov 2 12:54 CST.
note:
Nov 6 11:51 CST (coordinator audit, Explore sonnet; PR head reachable from origin/main): DONE, done check met on main.
The guard already exists on main: hooks/question_form.py option_letter_hit refuses 'option keyed none' on set, update and batch entries (rule option-letter-keys, step option-keys-are-letters, #898). So the Home session's proposal (a new rule) would be a second home; extend the existing one. Find first, unmeasured: why it did not fire. Likely: waiting_page_root judges a write only when the url is the cwd repo's waiting page (lint/layout.py is_waiting_page_url), so a write from another checkout, or a repo with no waiting-page key, is not judged; or the Home session ran an install older than Oct 31; or a `pick` of none, which this check does not read. Red first: a fixture of the write that went through is refused. Also: page.html's none-key block message (symbol NONE) names the option's label. Port: yes, the guard and the page are shared. Ready. Lane report-guard-slice-2 session_013NEJL3dNLxnmdt942Ffipw, started by the coordinator Nov 3 17:26 CST (batch 2); slice 2 also takes audit row pr1108-fixes.
